basis: Defined by hair and skin dysplasia and malformed, enamel-hypoplastic teeth; syndactyly is cutaneous rather than bony.
Bile acid biosynthesis disorder; cholestatic liver disease characterizes 7 of 9 described defects. Neurologic damage and malabsorption vary by subtype.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 30-79% and structural pes planus in 2/4 patients.
Defined by intellectual disability and neurologic dysfunction; overweight and short stature do not establish endocrine or skeletal damage.
Hormone-secreting tumor of the endocrine pancreas; exocrine pancreatic damage is not established across this group.
EBV infects B lymphocytes with characteristic blood and lymphoid/splenic involvement; transient pharyngeal symptoms and enzyme elevations alone do not establish additional damage.
Central movement disorder causing dystonia and parkinsonism; dysphagia and abnormal posture reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Congenital absence of distal phalanges is a defining skeletal malformation.
Villous adenocarcinoma commonly arises in intestinal villous adenomas, but this morphology is site-unspecified and includes reproductive-tract subtypes.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder defined by characteristic ECG abnormalities and susceptibility to ventricular arrhythmia.
Retinal degeneration, macular degeneration, nanophthalmos and glaucoma directly affect the eye; optic atrophy remains ocular.
Defined as a myopathy with muscle-fiber abnormalities and elevated CK, together with neural hyperexcitability, spasticity and pyramidal signs.
Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy with demyelination and axonal loss; weakness is neurogenic, and contracture frequency is unspecified.
Benign fibroepithelial tumor confined to the breast, which has no axis.
Congenital retinal phototransduction dysfunction causes stationary night blindness and abnormal electroretinography.
Autoinflammatory pustular skin disease; tongue changes 4/16, cholangitis 3/16 and arthritis below 30% do not support additional axes.
Autoimmune disease with common diagnostic arthritis and cutaneous lesions; intrinsic renal inflammation occurs in ~30-60%. Cytopenias and oral ulcers omitted by four-axis cap.
Suppurative infection involves the entire eye with scleral necrosis and possible orbital extension.
Renal tubular salt-wasting disorder defined by hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis; nephrocalcinosis is common. Additional lasting organ damage is not established.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic infiltration and inflammation directly affect the colon.
Developmental disability and ocular abnormalities define syndrome; sensorineural hearing impairment affects 2/4 patients.
Type Ib metabolic disease causes neutropenia and neutrophil dysfunction; hepatic glycogen storage with dysfunction occurs in >90%. Enterocolitis ~30-50% omitted by cap.
Abnormal elastic tissue produces localized dermal plaques; no systemic involvement is described.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are principal manifestations; cardiac, ocular, thyroid and esophageal defects lack evidence of frequency at least 30%.
Cardiac septation and limb defects define syndrome; nail dysplasia occurs in 3/5 and malformed teeth in 1/3, supporting skin and oral involvement.
